from.place: Current main-20261015 proof opening 'Choose a compactification c=(j,p)': arbitrary-site descent foundation for the affine-local compactification repair; bounded-below hypersheaf model steps 4-5: small hypercover test maps generate all cohomology-sheaf equivalences; the structural generation theorem is below the local-object characterization. Supporting primitive: Localized free Dold--Kan adjunction for module presheaves.

title: Localized free Dold--Kan adjunction for module presheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ given by covering sieves: a sieve is a set of arrows into an object closed under precomposition, the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. No fibre products or subcanonicity are assumed. Use [def-weil-size-convention] for universes and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] for associated sheaves.

Write $h_T(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,T)$. A hypercover $U_\bullet\to h_T$ is an augmented simplicial presheaf of sets whose terms are small coproducts of representables and whose augmented matching maps become epimorphisms after sheafification. The degree-zero matching presheaf is $h_T$; all higher matching presheaves, parametrizing compatible proper faces, are formed in presheaves. A refinement over $T$ means a morphism of augmented simplicial presheaves over $h_T$. A collection is dense if every hypercover over every $T$ admits a refinement by a member of that collection over the same $T$.

Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda)$, with unbounded cochains as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a hypercover $U_\bullet\to h_T$ write $L_T=\Lambda[h_T]$ and let $e_U:A_U\to L_T[0]$ be the alternating-face augmentation, where $A_U^{-n}=\Lambda[U_n]$ for $n\ge0$ and $A_U^r=0$ for $r>0$. Let $H$ be any small set of these hypercovers, not assumed dense, and let $B=\{e_U[k]:U\in H,\ k\in\mathbf Z\}$. Give $\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal P)$ its projective model and $B$-localized model [lem-cbc-dg-presheaf-model-localizations]. Give simplicial presheaves $\mathsf U(\mathcal C)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{sSet})$ their projective model and its left Bousfield localization at the augmentation maps in $H$ [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-localization-comparison], using simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set].

Let $N\Lambda$ take objectwise free simplicial $\Lambda$-modules, then their normalized nonnegative chain complexes $N_n=\bigcap_{i=1}^n\ker(d_i)$ with differential $d_0$, and reindex chain degree $n$ as cochain degree $-n$. Let $R(K)$ be the underlying simplicial presheaf of the Dold--Kan inverse of the nonnegative chain complex obtained by reindexing the smart truncation $\tau^{\le0}K$, whose term at $0$ is $\ker(d_K^0)$ and whose negative terms are those of $K$. These functors form an adjunction $N\Lambda\dashv R$ which is Quillen both for the projective models and for the localized models $\mathsf U(\mathcal C)_H\rightleftarrows\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal P)_B$.

The presheaf $R(K)$ is objectwise Kan and $\pi_m(R(K)(V),0)=H^{-m}(K(V))$ for $m\ge1$, while $\pi_0(R(K)(V))$ is the underlying set of $H^0(K(V))$. Translations identify the homotopy groups at any other vertex with those at zero, naturally on the corresponding slice site. The functor $R$ sends every cohomology-sheaf equivalence of complexes to a local weak equivalence of simplicial presheaves. A Kan complex is a simplicial set with fillers for all horns. The standard simplex $\Delta^n$ is the simplicial set represented by $[n]$, its boundary $\partial\Delta^n$ is the union of its proper faces, and a horn is the union of all faces except one. For objectwise Kan simplicial presheaves, a local weak equivalence means an isomorphism on the associated sheaves of $\pi_0$ and, for every $V\in\mathcal C$, vertex $x\in X(V)_0$ and $m\ge1$, an isomorphism on the associated sheaves on $\mathcal C/V$ of the homotopy groups $\pi_m(X|_{\mathcal C/V},x)\to\pi_m(Y|_{\mathcal C/V},f(x))$. Here $\mathcal C/V$ has the induced covering-sieve topology.

For every $T$, the map $N\Lambda(h_T\times\partial\Delta^1)\to N\Lambda(h_T\times\Delta^1)$ is the inclusion $L_T[0]\oplus L_T[0]\to I_T$, where $I_T^{-1}=L_T$, $I_T^0=L_T\oplus L_T$, its differential sends $a$ to $(-a,a)$, and all other terms vanish. Thus the endpoint inclusion is identified under the same adjunction, including its maps, with the simplicial boundary inclusion.

source.place: Choudhury--Gallauer, Proposition 3.15 and Lemma 5.12 with its proof, pp. 10, 20; the explicit normalized interval and its endpoint inclusion in the proof of Lemma 5.13, pp. 20-21; cochain reindexing of their homological convention.

proof.text: For a simplicial presheaf $X$ and a complex $K$, a chain map $N\Lambda X\to K$ factors uniquely through $\tau^{\le0}K$: the degree-zero component must land in $\ker(d_K^0)$, and all negative-degree components are unchanged. Here $\mathsf{sMod}_\Lambda$ denotes simplicial $\Lambda$-modules. Apply the normalization equivalence of [lem-cbc-dold-kan-homology] objectwise and the free-module universal property degreewise to obtain natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Ch}}(N\Lambda X,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{sMod}_\Lambda)}(\Lambda[X],\Gamma tK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf U(\mathcal C)}(X,RK)$. The bijections commute with the restriction maps, since all three constructions are functorial. This proves the claimed adjunction.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, §3.3, sequence (1), Fact 3.14(3) and Proposition 3.15, printed pp. 11–12; smart truncation and natural presheaf adjunction.

proof.text: Evaluate $K$ at $V$. Its smart truncation reindexes to the complex $t(K(V))$ of [lem-cbc-dold-kan-homology]. That node gives Kan fillers, the natural formulas $\pi_0R(K)(V)\cong H^0(K(V))$ and $\pi_m(R(K)(V),0)\cong H^{-m}(K(V))$, and translation at every vertex. For $x\in R(K)(V)_0$, restrict $x$ along each arrow $W\to V$; subtracting that restricted vertex defines the translation on the whole slice site, so these identifications commute with its restriction maps.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, Fact 3.14(4) and the final sentence of the proof of Lemma 5.12, printed pp. 11, 20; restriction and translation at all slice basepoints.

proof.text: Let $f:K\to L$ induce isomorphisms on every cohomology sheaf. By [lem-cbc-module-sheafification-underlying-sets], the underlying set maps of $H^0(f)$ become isomorphisms after set sheafification, so step 2 proves the required $\pi_0$ assertion. For any $V$ and $m\ge1$, [lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification] identifies the sheafification of the restriction of $H^{-m}(f)$ to $\mathcal C/V$ with the restriction of its sheafification. This is an isomorphism by hypothesis. Apply [lem-cbc-module-sheafification-underlying-sets] also on this slice to identify its underlying set map with the set sheafification of the restricted cohomology map; it is an isomorphism, and the compatible abelian group operations give the same isomorphism as group sheaves. Step 2 identifies it with the homotopy-sheaf map at zero. Its translation by each restricted vertex identifies it with the map at any specified $x$. These are exactly all tests in the definition of local weak equivalence stated above.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, Proof of Lemma 5.12, second claim, printed p. 20; expanded using underlying-set and slice sheafification comparisons.

proof.text: Suppose $f:K\to L$ is a projective fibration of complexes, thus degreewise surjective at every object by [lem-cbc-dg-presheaf-model-localizations]. For $m>0$, the degree-m map of the normalized chains of $R(f)(V)$ is $f^{-m}(V)$, since smart truncation changes only degree zero. Hence [lem-cbc-simplicial-module-model] implies that $R(f)(V)$ is a Kan fibration. If $f$ is also an objectwise quasi-isomorphism, the same node's normalized weak-equivalence criterion gives that $R(f)(V)$ is a weak equivalence (its normalized homology in all nonnegative degrees is $H^{-m}(f(V))$). The source projective fibrations and trivial fibrations are objectwise by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. Thus $R$ preserves projective fibrations and trivial fibrations, so step 1 is a projective Quillen adjunction. Objectwise weak homotopy equivalences $g$ of simplicial presheaves are sent by $N\Lambda$ to objectwise quasi-isomorphisms: this is the final assertion of [lem-cbc-simplicial-module-model] at each $V$.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, §3.3, transferred-model paragraph before Proposition 3.15 and its proof, printed pp. 11–12; objectwise right Quillen check.

proof.text: For an augmentation $s:U_\bullet\to h_T$ in $H$, apply [lem-cbc-normalized-alternating-homotopy-equivalence] at every object $V$ to the simplicial module $\Lambda[U_\bullet(V)]$. Naturality assembles these inclusions into a map of complex presheaves. Each evaluated inclusion is a chain homotopy equivalence; consequently the assembled map is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism: $dh+hd$ induces zero on homology because on a cycle it is the boundary $d(hz)$. The composite $N\Lambda(U_\bullet)\to A_U\xrightarrow{e_U}L_T[0]$ is $N\Lambda(s)$, since in degree zero the inclusion is the identity and augmentations commute with faces. As $e_U\in B$, this composite is a weak equivalence in the B-localized complex model by [lem-cbc-dg-presheaf-model-localizations]. Let $Q$ be functorial projective cofibrant replacement of simplicial presheaves, available by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. Its objectwise weak equivalences $QX\to X$ remain objectwise quasi-isomorphisms under $N\Lambda$ by step 4. In the natural square comparing $N\Lambda Q(s)$ with $N\Lambda(s)$, both vertical arrows and the lower horizontal arrow are therefore B-localized weak equivalences. Two-out-of-three proves the same for $N\Lambda Q(s)$, without any projective-cofibrancy assumption on $U_\bullet$.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, Proof of Lemma 5.12, first claim, printed p. 20; Fact 3.14(1) and derived-generator check via functorial cofibrant replacement.

proof.text: The identity from projective complexes to the B-localized model is left Quillen by [lem-cbc-dg-presheaf-model-localizations]; compose it with step 4. The source projective simplicial-presheaf model is simplicial by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model], its H-localization exists with the mapping-space convention of [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-localization-comparison], and step 5 verifies the image-of-cofibrant-replacement hypothesis for every $s\in H$. Apply [lem-coef-bousfield-quillen-descent] to this adjunction and target the B-localized complex model. It gives exactly $N\Lambda:\mathsf U(\mathcal C)_H\rightleftarrows\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal P)_B:R$ as a Quillen adjunction. Only $e_U[0]\in B$ is needed here; all shifts cause no obstruction. No density assumption has been used.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, Proof of Lemma 5.12, first claim, printed p. 20; localization universal property made explicit by the cited Bousfield Quillen descent lemma.

proof.text: Compute the normalized free interval object at $V$ and put $L=L_T(V)$. The degree-zero term is $L v_0\oplus L v_1$. In degree one the basis is $v_0,e=[01],v_1$ with $d_1(e)=v_0$ and $d_1(v_i)=v_i$; thus $\ker d_1$ is the copy of $L$ generated by $e-s_0v_0$. Its $d_0$ is $v_1-v_0$, giving $a\mapsto(-a,a)$. For $n\ge2$, write the n-simplex basis as the two constant simplices and cuts $e_j=0^{j+1}1^{n-j}$ ($0\le j<n$). The kernel of $d_n$ is generated by $e_{n-1}-v_0$, and $d_{n-1}$ sends this to $e_{n-2}-v_0$, a difference of distinct basis vectors. Hence $\ker d_n\cap\ker d_{n-1}=0$ and the normalized degree-n term vanishes. The boundary has only the two constant vertices; its normalized complex is $L[0]\oplus L[0]$, and its map into the interval sends them to $v_0,v_1$. These calculations commute with restriction in $V$, proving the claimed complexes and the actual endpoint inclusion for $L_T$. The bijections of step 1 therefore identify squares with this map on the left with squares with the simplicial boundary inclusion on the left, retaining both endpoint maps.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, Proof of Lemma 5.13, interval paragraph, printed pp. 20–21; direct basis calculation in the opposite-face normalization.

proof_origin.place: Source-guided reconstruction of Proposition 3.15 and Lemmas 5.12–5.13, with cochain reindexing and the explicit interval calculation.
